event: Phishing email delivered to a Warehouse & Ops supervisor; credentials for user0147 harvested via a fake VPN login page (the same account later confirmed compromised in the Log Analysis / Intrusion Detection case)
Attacker authenticates to the VPN gateway using user0147's stolen credentials from an external IP
Attacker enumerates internal file shares reachable from the Warehouse VLAN; identifies the WMS integration server and a general-purpose file server
Attacker escalates privileges on the file server using a cached local admin credential left over from a vendor support visit 8 months earlier
Attacker stages ransomware payload and begins exfiltrating a sample of shared-drive files (double-extortion staging)
Automated alert fires: anomalous after-hours data volume leaving the file server to an unfamiliar external IP
Analyst begins triage; confirms the traffic is not a known backup job and escalates to the on-call incident commander
Declares a P1 security incident; isolates the file server from the network (pulls its switch port) and disables user0147's account domain-wide
VPN session for user0147 is force-terminated; VPN gateway blocks the attacker's source IP; all active sessions for the account are killed
Team discovers ransomware encryption has already begun on 2 of 6 shared-drive volumes before containment completed
Malicious payload and persistence mechanisms removed from the file server; server rebuilt from a known-good image rather than cleaned in place
Full credential reset forced for all Warehouse & Ops accounts as a precaution
Encrypted volumes restored from the previous night's backup (4 hours of data loss on those 2 volumes)
File server returned to production after a clean rebuild; monitoring intensified for 72 hours post-incident
Tabletop debrief convened; timeline reconstructed and gaps identified (see After-Action Report)
